elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: M&I must “defend Customer,” and the supplied definition of Customer expressly includes its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: M&I indemnifies Customer for liabilities or expenses arising from enumerated third-party claims; Customer includes its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B(i) covers third-party claims that the Services or M&I software infringe a U.S. patent, copyright, or trademark.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Coverage is limited to laws protecting protected classes and specified discrimination or harassment matters, not M&I's breach of applicable law generally.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly cover claims arising from M&I's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 requires the indemnitee to give notice of the claim, including a brief description of its amount and basis if known.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: The indemnifying party may assume control of the defense with counsel reasonably satisfactory to the indemnitee.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The indemnitee must cooperate fully and assist in the defense “in all reasonable respects.”

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered language imposes no Customer indemnity, and therefore contains no Customer indemnity extending beyond the permitted categories.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B(i) indemnifies Customer for third-party claims that the Services or M&I software infringe U.S. patents, copyrights, or trademarks.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion is included; the permissive element allows but does not require such an exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: No Customer-combination exclusion is included; the permissive element allows but does not require such an exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification exclusion is included; the permissive element allows but does not require such an exclusion.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: M&I must, at its option, procure continued use or modify or replace the infringing item so it is non-infringing.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: If none of those remedies is reasonably available, M&I must refund the fees paid for the infringing item.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: M&I's total liability under Paragraph B is capped at three times annual fees, and Section 13.4 begins with an exception for Section 14.2(C).
